note: Title matches partsavatar and repairpal listings seen in search. Driver-assist (adaptive cruise) code, not an engine fault; any radar replacement or bumper work needs calibration. obd-codes.com has no page.

m: On a diesel with DEF, the computer found a broken (open) circuit to the heater that keeps the DEF from freezing. The emissions system may be disabled and the truck may eventually limit speed or power.
c: Failed DEF heater (often part of the tank/pump assembly)
Broken wire or bad connector in the heater circuit
Blown fuse or relay in the heater circuit
SCR control module fault
note: Diesel SCR/DEF systems only (Chevrolet/GMC complaints likely Duramax).

t: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit Range/Performance
m: The circuit for the valve that regulates how much fuel the high-pressure pump delivers is reading out of range. Fuel pressure can be wrong, causing hard starts, no-start, stalling or reduced power.
c: Faulty fuel volume regulator (metering) valve
Wiring short, open or corroded connector
High-pressure fuel pump problem
Engine computer fault (rare)
note: Mainly common-rail diesels and gasoline direct-injection engines (Mercedes complaints likely BlueTEC diesels).

t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit Range/Performance
m: The transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch 'G' is reporting values the computer doesn't expect. Shift quality changes, and the transmission may go into limp mode (starting in 2nd or 3rd gear).
c: Failed transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch
Open or shorted wiring in the sensor circuit
Internal hydraulic problem (leak, valve body)
Transmission control module fault (rare)

t: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
m: The second fuel pressure sensor's reading doesn't make sense to the computer. The engine may be hard to start, not start, or run poorly.
c: Faulty fuel pressure sensor B
Real fuel delivery problem (weak pump, clogged filter)
Damaged wiring or loose connector
Engine computer fault (rare)
note: Which sensor is 'B' (low- or high-pressure side) depends on the engine.

t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit
m: The circuit for transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch 'H' has an electrical fault. Shift quality changes and the transmission may go into limp mode.
c: Failed pressure sensor/switch H
Open or short in the sensor wiring
Internal transmission problem affecting the sensor
Transmission control module fault (rare)
note: Mitsubishi complaints likely relate to its CVT.

m: In a dual-clutch or automated manual transmission, clutch B stays engaged when the computer wants it released. The car can lurch, shudder, stall when stopping or refuse to shift.
c: Worn or contaminated clutch (fluid leak onto it)
Faulty clutch B actuator or release mechanism
Clutch not adapted/relearned after service
Transmission control module fault
note: Dual-clutch/automated manual only (Ford PowerShift DPS6; clutch B drives the even gears and reverse). Title matches mycarly and obdguide listings seen in search. obd-codes.com has no page.

t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Low
m: The computer sees too-low voltage (often a short to ground) in the circuit that controls coolant bypass valve A. The engine may warm slowly, run at the wrong temperature or give weak heat.
c: Failed coolant control valve (Subaru thermo control valve)
Coolant vapor getting into the valve's electronics
Wiring short to ground or damaged connector
Engine computer fault (rare)
note: Title matches partsavatar listing seen in search. Subaru TSB 09-80-21 (P2682 and P26Ax, thermo control valve design change) covers 2019-21 Forester, 2020-21 Legacy/Outback, 2021 Crosstrek. obd-codes.com has no page.

t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
m: The position sensor inside coolant bypass valve A is giving readings the computer doesn't expect. Engine temperature control can be off, with slow warm-up or weak heat.
c: Failed coolant control valve or its built-in position sensor
Coolant vapor or leaks damaging the sensor
Wiring or connector problem
Engine computer fault (rare)
note: On Subaru it is part of the thermo control valve failures covered by TSB 09-80-21 (2019-21 Forester, 2020-21 Legacy/Outback, 2021 Crosstrek). One Q&A site calls it a heater valve code; Subaru sources tie it to the thermo control valve. obd-codes.com has no page.

t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
m: The speed sensor on the transmission's intermediate shaft is giving readings that don't fit what the computer expects. Shifting can become harsh or erratic and the transmission may go into a backup mode.
c: Faulty intermediate shaft speed sensor
Wiring or connector problem to the sensor
Low or dirty transmission fluid
Transmission or engine control module fault

m: In an automated manual or dual-clutch transmission, the computer found an electrical fault in the position circuit for shift fork A (the fork for the odd gears on Ford's DPS6). Gears may not engage, shifting can be erratic or the car may not move.
c: Failing transmission control module (houses the position sensors on Ford DPS6)
Wiring, connector or ground problem
Shift motor fault
Internal shift mechanism damage
note: Dual-clutch/automated manual only (Ford PowerShift DPS6). Title matches go-parts and forum listings seen in search. obd-codes.com has no page.

m: The transmission computer commanded Park but could not confirm that the transmission actually went into Park. The driver may see a warning to shift to Park or set the parking brake, and the car may not stay put on its own.
c: Fault in the park mechanism or park actuator
Park position sensor or wiring fault
Low or dirty transmission fluid
Transmission control module fault
note: obd-codes.com has no page for this code (404). Carly states the title but gives no causes; causes above are general. Some auto-generated sites list unrelated meanings (camshaft, O2 sensor); ignore those.

t: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High Bank 1
m: The engine computer sees a voltage that is too high from the sensor that reports where the intake runner flaps are, on bank 1. The driver may notice the check engine light, a little less power and worse fuel economy.
c: Failed intake runner position sensor or actuator
Wiring or connector fault in the sensor circuit
Faulty runner control relay (if fitted)
Engine computer fault (rare)

t: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit/Open
m: The engine computer found a break or fault in the circuit it uses to control the fuel pump module. The car may be hard to start, stall, run weakly, or not start at all.
c: Failed fuel pump or fuel pump module
Broken or damaged wiring to the pump module
Corroded or loose connector
Engine control module fault
note: obd-codes.com writes the title without the 'A'; newer SAE lists include the 'A'.

t: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Range/Performance
m: The engine and transmission computers share a signal about how much torque the engine is making, and that signal does not make sense. Shifts can feel wrong or harsh, and the car may go into a reduced-power mode.
c: Wiring fault between the engine and transmission computers
Engine control module fault or old software
Transmission control module fault
note: obd-codes.com has no page for this code (404).

m: The transmission was asked to go into Reverse but the computer could not confirm that it did. The car may not back up, or the transmission may go into a limited limp mode.
c: Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Faulty shift solenoid
Blocked hydraulic passage in the transmission
Wiring, connector or transmission computer fault

t: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too Low
m: The engine computer has pushed its fuel pressure control as far as it can go and the pressure is still lower than it wants. The engine may lose power, run poorly, or stall.
c: Weak or failing fuel pump
Clogged fuel filter
Fuel leak or faulty pressure regulator
Faulty fuel pressure sensor reading low
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404). Search results also show an NHTSA TSB (static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2022/MC-10213671-0001.pdf) using the same title for 2018-2020 common rail diesels; not opened. One auto-generated site calls it a pressure sensor circuit fault, which disagrees and looks unreliable.

m: The transmission computer saw that the hydraulic pressure on clutch A did not drop the way it should when that clutch was released. Shifts may feel off, and the check engine light comes on.
c: Faulty clutch pressure control solenoid
Low transmission fluid
Valve body or hydraulic pressure problem
Wiring or connector fault
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404). Some sites add '/Too Low' to the end of the title.

t: Body Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
m: The body control module asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light because it found a fault of its own. The light itself is the main symptom; the real problem is stored in the body control module.
c: A fault stored in the body control module
Body control module wiring or software issue
Communication problem between the body and engine computers
note: Only one loading source (Carly) states this title; obd-codes.com has no page (404). Causes are general, since Carly lists none. Unusual for a generic P0 code: scan the body control module for its own codes.

t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Low
m: The engine computer sees a voltage that is too low from the sensor that reports the position of the coolant bypass (coolant control) valve. The check engine light comes on, and engine warm-up or heat control may not work right.
c: Failed coolant bypass valve or its internal position sensor
Broken internal gear in the coolant valve
Wiring short or open in the sensor circuit
Poor connector contact
note: Source is Stellantis TSB 07-009-23 (2022-2023 Ram 1500 3.6L, cracked gear in the 3-way coolant valve; fix = replace valve). The TSB writes the title without 'A'. obd-codes.com has no page (404). The complaints are mostly Subaru, which uses a similar electric coolant control valve.

t: Coolant Temperature Relapsed Below Diagnostic Monitoring Temperature
m: The engine warmed up enough for its self-tests, then the coolant temperature dropped back below that level. Often the only sign is the check engine light, sometimes with a weak heater.
c: Thermostat stuck open
Faulty coolant temperature sensor
Cooling fan running when it should not
Very cold weather or short trips
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404).

t: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Open
m: The engine computer checks that its main power relay is feeding it voltage, and that check circuit reads open. The car may be slow to start or not start, and some electrical items may stop working.
c: Failed engine computer power relay
Blown fuse or fusible link
Open or shorted wire between the relay and the computer

t: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit
m: The engine computer found a problem in the circuit of the sensor that reports where the turbo's boost control (wastegate or vane) is. The engine may feel weak or hesitate, and fuel economy can drop.
c: Failed boost control position sensor
Open or shorted signal wire
Lost power or ground at the sensor
Engine computer fault (rare)
note: obd-codes.com shortens 'Turbocharger' to 'Turbo'. Newer SAE lists use 'Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Sensor Circuit'.

m: On a diesel, the computer decided the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) is not cleaning the exhaust the way good fluid should. Emissions rise and, if not fixed, the truck may limit its speed or power.
c: Contaminated, diluted or old DEF
Faulty DEF injector
Failing SCR catalyst
Faulty DEF quality sensor or NOx sensor
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404). Diesel only.

t: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
m: On a diesel, the sensor that reads the temperature of the diesel exhaust fluid tank is sending a voltage that is too low. The exhaust cleaning system may not work right and the check engine light comes on.
c: Failed DEF tank temperature sensor
Shorted or open sensor wiring
SCR control module or engine computer fault
note: Diesel only.

m: On a diesel, the reading from the diesel exhaust fluid level sensor does not make sense. The DEF gauge may be wrong or show low fluid when the tank is full.
c: Failed DEF level sensor
Float or level arm stuck
Wrong fluid in the DEF tank
Wiring short or connector fault
note: Diesel only.

t: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit High
m: The sensor that reports where the turbo's boost control is sits at a voltage that is too high. The engine may feel weak or hesitate, and fuel economy can drop.
c: Failed boost control position sensor (most common)
Signal wire shorted to voltage
Open ground at the sensor
Engine computer fault (rare)
note: obd-codes.com shortens 'Turbocharger' to 'Turbo'. Newer SAE lists use 'Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Sensor Circuit High'.

t: Pressure Control Solenoid G Control Circuit Range/Performance
m: The transmission computer sees that pressure control solenoid G is not working the way it commands. Shifts may slip or feel harsh, and the transmission may go into limp mode or run hot.
c: Failed pressure control solenoid G
Dirty or low transmission fluid, or clogged filter
Valve body fault
Wiring or connector damage
note: Search results say Nissan CVT manuals call solenoid G the 'select solenoid'; not checked on a Nissan source.

m: The computer sees too little vacuum in the brake booster, which helps you press the brake pedal. The pedal can feel hard and take more effort to stop the car.
c: Leaking brake booster
Cracked or loose vacuum hose
Faulty one-way check valve or brake vacuum sensor
Low engine vacuum or failing vacuum pump

m: On a hybrid, the computer found a fault in the module that runs the motor-generator used to start the engine and charge the battery. The hybrid system may shut down or not work.
c: Failed starter/generator control module
Module software needs an update
Wiring or connector fault
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404). Hybrid/electrified vehicles only. Newer SAE lists may add 'A' to the title.

t: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Pressure Sensor Performance
m: The computer uses a pressure sensor to check that the crankcase vent hose is connected and working, and that sensor's reading does not make sense. Usually only the check engine light comes on.
c: Water or ice from condensation in the sensor or hose (cold, short trips)
Failed crankcase pressure sensor
Disconnected, split or blocked vent hose
Sensor wiring or connector fault
note: GM TechLink article covers some 2019 CT6; 2019-2022 XT4; 2020-2022 CT4, CT5, XT5, XT6, Blazer, Acadia; 2021-2022 Envision with the 2.0L turbo (RPO LSY). Fix often = thaw and dry the sensor and hose. obd-codes.com has no page (404); obdguide uses 'Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Range/Performance'.

m: In 9th gear, the transmission's input and output speeds do not match the ratio 9th gear should give, so the computer thinks it is slipping or in the wrong gear. The driver may feel slipping, flare or harsh shifts.
c: Low or contaminated transmission fluid
Worn clutches for 9th gear
Faulty shift solenoid or valve body
Faulty transmission speed sensor
note: Applies to 9- and 10-speed automatics. obd-codes.com has no page (404).

m: On a hybrid, the computer found that the inverter that controls the generator is not working as it should. The high-voltage hybrid system may shut down.
c: Failed inverter/converter assembly
High-voltage control module fault
Wiring or connector fault
Inverter cooling problem
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404). Hybrid vehicles only.

t: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
m: On engines that use oil pressure to fire the injectors (mainly diesels), the sensor that reads that oil pressure reads too low. The engine may be hard to start or not start.
c: Failed injector control pressure (ICP) sensor
Low oil level or oil pump problem
Damaged wiring, bad ground or corroded connector
Blown fuse or engine computer fault
note: Mostly Ford Power Stroke and other oil-actuated injector diesels.

m: On a hybrid, the inverter that controls the generator is running too hot. The hybrid system may cut power to protect itself.
c: Low coolant in the inverter cooling loop
Failed inverter coolant pump
Clogged radiator or bad cooling fan
Failed inverter/converter assembly
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404). Hybrid vehicles only.

t: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High
m: The computer sees a voltage that is too high in the circuit that controls fuel shutoff valve A. The check engine light comes on; other symptoms depend on the engine.
c: Wiring shorted to voltage in the valve control circuit
Failed fuel shutoff valve
Connector fault
Engine computer fault
note: obd-codes.com notes there is little detailed information on this code; causes are general circuit causes.

t: System Too Lean at Idle Bank 1
m: At idle, the engine on bank 1 is getting too much air for the fuel it gets. The idle may be rough, the engine can misfire, and it may be hard to start when hot.
c: Vacuum or intake air leak (hoses, brake booster line, PCV)
Dirty or faulty mass airflow sensor
Weak fuel pump, clogged filter or bad regulator
Leaking EVAP purge valve or exhaust leak before the O2 sensor

t: Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Stuck Open
m: The coolant bypass (coolant control) valve is stuck open and does not move when the computer commands it. The engine and transmission may not hold the right temperature, and the check engine light comes on.
c: Failed coolant bypass valve
Engine computer software needs an update
Poor electrical connection at the valve
Ground wire problem
note: KBB writes 'Stuck/Open'. obd-codes.com has no page (404). Related Ram 3.6L coolant valve TSB: static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2023/MC-10243239-9999.pdf (lists P26A3/P26A6/P2681, not P26AB).

m: The computer sees a voltage that is too low in the circuit for the fuel injector on cylinder 4. The engine may run rough, lose power and use more fuel.
c: Faulty fuel injector
Open or short in the injector wiring
Loose or corroded connector
Clogged injector
note: obd-codes.com uses the older title without 'A'.

t: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
m: The transmission computer gets no signal from the sensor that measures the speed of the intermediate shaft. Shifts may be harsh, and other warning lights or limp mode may follow.
c: Failed intermediate shaft speed sensor
Wiring or connector fault
Low or dirty transmission fluid
Transmission computer fault

t: Active Grille Air Shutter A Stuck On
m: The movable shutters in the front grille that open and close to manage airflow are stuck and not moving as commanded. The check engine light comes on; warm-up can be slower, and in hot driving the engine may get less cooling air.
c: Broken or jammed grille shutter
Failed shutter motor (actuator)
Ice, snow or debris blocking the shutters
Wiring or connector fault
note: Carly spells it 'Grill'. obd-codes.com has no page (404).

t: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
m: The sensor that tells the computer the transmission is in Park is sending a voltage that is too high. The car may not start, may be hard to shift out of Park, or the starter may work in the wrong gear.
c: Failed park position sensor or switch
Damaged wiring
Corroded or loose connector
Engine or transmission computer fault

m: The transmission was asked to go into 1st gear but the computer could not confirm that it did. The car may pull away weakly, go into limp mode or limit its speed.
c: Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Faulty shift solenoid
Blocked hydraulic passage
Wiring, connector or transmission computer fault

t: EVAP System High Load Purge Line A Performance
m: The fuel vapor system has a separate purge line used when a turbo engine is under boost, and the computer found that line is not working right. Usually only the check engine light comes on, sometimes with a fuel smell.
c: Cracked, disconnected or blocked purge line
Faulty purge valve or check valve
Damaged ejector (venturi) in the purge line
Loose fuel cap or other EVAP leak
note: Sources disagree on wording: KBB and obdguide use 'High Load Purge Line A Performance'; Carly uses 'High Pressure Purge Line Performance'. Same meaning. obd-codes.com has no page (404).

t: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
m: The second fuel pressure sensor (sensor B) is sending a voltage that is too low. The engine may be hard to start, not start, or feel weak.
c: Failed fuel pressure sensor B
Low fuel pressure from a weak pump or clogged filter
Wiring short or open
Engine computer fault

m: On a hybrid or EV, the computer found a fault with the precharge contactor, a relay that eases high voltage on gently before the main battery relays close. The car may not go into Ready mode or the hybrid system may shut off.
c: Failed precharge contactor or its resistor
Weak 12-volt battery
High-voltage control module fault
Wiring or connector fault
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404). Newer SAE lists use 'Hybrid/EV Battery Precharge Contactor Circuit'.

m: The high-voltage battery's voltage is jumping around more than it should. Power may be limited, fuel economy may drop, and the hybrid system may shut down.
c: Weak or failing battery cells
Cell balancing problem
Battery control module fault
Loose or corroded high-voltage connection or wiring
note: obd-codes.com has no page (404). Hybrid/EV only.

t: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
m: The circuit the engine computer uses to check its main power relay reads too low. The car may be slow to start or not start, and some electrical items may not work.
c: Failed engine computer power relay
Blown fuse or fusible link
Open or shorted wire between the relay and the computer

t: NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1 Catalyst 2
m: On a diesel, the computer found that the second exhaust catalyst (the SCR catalyst that uses DEF) is not removing enough NOx. The check engine light comes on and emissions are higher.
c: Engine computer software issue (fixed by an update on some trucks)
Low or poor-quality DEF
Faulty NOx sensor
DEF crystal deposits or a worn SCR catalyst
note: Source is GM bulletin 22-NA-243 (2022 Silverado/Sierra 1500 3.0L diesel, RPO J22): cause = software, fix = ECM update plus NOx sensor and reductant loading resets. obdguide adds 'SCR' to the title. A forum post says older code lists show P2C7A as reserved, so older scanners may not name it. obd-codes.com has no page (404).

m: The voltage differs too much between the sections of the high-voltage battery pack. Fuel economy and electric range may drop, and the hybrid system may limit power.
c: Weak or failing battery cells or modules
Cell balancing problem
Battery control module fault
Bad high-voltage connection or wiring
note: RepairPal writes 'Hybrid Battery Pack Voltage Variation'; Carly uses 'Hybrid/EV'. obd-codes.com has no page (404). Plug-in hybrid/EV only (complaints are Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid and Jeep 4xe).

t: Injector Control Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
m: While the engine is cranking, the oil pressure used to fire the injectors (mainly on diesels) is too low, so the engine may not start. Smoke or odd engine noises can also show up.
c: Low engine oil level or oil pressure
Leak in the high-pressure oil system
Faulty injection pressure regulator or sensor
Open or shorted control wiring
note: Mostly Ford Power Stroke and other oil-actuated injector diesels.

m: The transmission computer found a fault with pressure control solenoid D, which sets hydraulic pressure for shifting. Shifts may slip or feel harsh, and the transmission may go into limp mode or run hot.
c: Failed pressure control solenoid D
Dirty fluid or clogged filter
Valve body or pump problem
Wiring or connector damage
note: obd-codes.com adds 'Malfunction' to the title (older style); the SAE base title is just 'Pressure Control Solenoid D'.
